solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: A question about who might lend a hand to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the abbreviation M plus a word for help also spell out the domestic servant who gives help.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant is employed to give help, and the letters split as a male sign plus assistance.

clue.text: Expert regarding US first lady, I may appear in a film

indicators.note: these letters show up inside the phrase a film

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen as first lady of the land
can means may, be permitted to

explanation.surface: A US first lady hopes for a part in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US first lady' tempts towards a president's wife; 'US' belongs to the definition, and the first lady is the Queen. 'appear in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who specialises in the history and culture of the United States is called this.

clue.text: Crazy about a picture of Middle Eastern city

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: mad means crazy
a scene is a picture or view

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about an image of a city in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MAD into DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene describes something from Damascus, the Syrian capital.

indicators.note: the word tear is placed inside the run made by top and worker's

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
ants are the classic worker insects; the possessive gives the S
to rip is to tear

explanation.surface: A rip has appeared in the best worker's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top worker' reads as a leading employee, but the two words split apart and the tear sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri pants are close-fitting calf-length trousers, named after the Italian island.

clue.text: Below heart of local battle site is small tree

indicators.note: in a down entry the battle site comes below the first letter
the heart of a word is its central letter, here of local

parts.note: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles

explanation.surface: A small tree stands beneath the centre of a local battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below' puts YPRES under the C from local, as the entry runs downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a tall dark evergreen conifer often planted in cemeteries.

clue.text: On a Friday, a lot excitedly left work

indicators.note: in a down entry the rearranged letters come on top of, that is just after, the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Late in the week, a lot of people left the office in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left work' reads as leaving the office; left is PORT and work is the definition. 'excitedly' rearranges A FRIDAY A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Henry James novel about Isabel Archer is a celebrated literary work.

parts.note: the future is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A warning that things will turn violent later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in future' reads as later on, but the future is a grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense emotions or storms are extreme in force, much like violent ones.

clue.text: In my opinion, an upstanding woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

explanation.surface: A personal verdict that someone is an honest, decent woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like praise of the woman; it reverses IMO AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, as in the Book of Ruth.

indicators.note: the final letter of leaves is taken

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A child finally leaves home for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child or baby.

clue.text: Drink — minute alcoholic one — which brings people together?

parts.note: tea is a common drink
a spirit is a strong alcoholic drink such as gin or whisky

explanation.surface: An office drink, then a tiny tot of liquor, offered as a way to bond the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared sense of loyalty and cooperation is what unites the members of a group.

indicators.note: the combined letters are read backwards
taking every other letter of the word group, the second and fourth

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual books

explanation.surface: A party regularly books a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Group, and 'return' turns the whole run around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey or trip taken for pleasure, visiting several places.

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of topical

parts.note: an issue is a subject or topic under discussion

explanation.surface: A newspaper's opening piece on a topical subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper's' suggests a newspaper, but the definition is thin paper; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, as in tissue paper or a paper handkerchief.

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling or offensive

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: lingo is informal for a language or jargon

explanation.surface: Swearing, even in short bursts, gets under people's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps irritating or embittering someone, so it is causing annoyance.

clue.text: Fruit and rindless Brie with crackers — beneficial to digestion

parts.note: a nut is a dry fruit

indicators.note: taking the rind off removes the outer letters of Brie

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad, as is mental

explanation.surface: A cheese board of fruit and peeled Brie on crackers, sold as good for the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits for the cheese; it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nutrimental is nourishing, providing food the body can digest and use.

clue.text: Deal with five o'clock shadow? Not hard for husband

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: five o'clock shadow is late-day stubble, which you deal with by shaving
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Advice on tackling stubble, apparently addressed to a married man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' looks like a man who shaves; it is the verb, as in husbanding your resources. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband money or supplies is to manage them thriftily, that is, to conserve them.

clue.text: One devouring fruit simpered pathetically after eating it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the word it inside them
pathetically suggests something feeble and in disarray, so the letters of simpered are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats fruit and then simpers pathetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pathetically' rearranges the letters into SPIDERME, and 'after eating' puts the other word inside, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny arachnid is a garden pest that feeds on the leaves of fruit trees and plants.

indicators.note: the reversed word surrounds and so hampers the speaker
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Postponements finish up tying a public speaker's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' reads as finish; it is a goal, which 'up' turns into MIA in the down entry, and 'hampering' wraps it round the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria, plural of moratorium, are temporary suspensions or authorised postponements.

clue.text: Prepare to blow up rock, getting right in the soup

parts.note: to mine an area is to lay explosives ready to blow it up

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for rock

parts.note: stone is rock

explanation.surface: A demolition plan that ends with someone landed in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' is an idiom for in trouble, but here 'the soup' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, often with pasta.

indicators.note: the birds' word goes around the other letters

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
hep is dated slang for in or fashionable, like hip

explanation.surface: Birds flying about in underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang pants means rubbish or dreadful, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: The pits is slang for the worst possible thing, just as pants means awful.

clue.text: Siren in French bank cashier initially stops

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: the cashier's first letter blocks up, so sits inside, the word for bank

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

indicators.note: the first letter of cashier is taken

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off in a French bank as the cashier stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' and 'cashier' paint a bank raid; bank is TIER, with C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman who lures others, which is what an enticer does.

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, the letters between the ends of wine

explanation.surface: Checking on what is in the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, as a rider pulls the reins to slow a horse.

clue.text: Groups of experts, heading off back round the Atlantic island

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the word the
the trimmed word is read backwards
the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: panels are groups of experts brought together to judge or advise

explanation.surface: Expert committees, decapitated and sent back, surround an Atlantic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ANELS, 'back' gives SLENA, and 'round' puts that around the article.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helena is a remote British island in the South Atlantic, where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Russian dogs you had once banned in Greek island

indicators.note: banned means these letters are excluded

parts.note: Samoyeds are white Siberian sled dogs
ye'd is an archaic contraction of ye had

explanation.surface: Russian dog breeds that were once kept off a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean Sea, birthplace of Pythagoras.

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: haste means hurry
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone has to rush off soon, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' reads as soon but signals cutting the end off HASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Has to and must both express obligation, as in she must go.

parts.note: Tut is Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian boy king
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch called Edward made a disapproving noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Edward' reads as one English monarch, but it splits into Tutankhamun and a pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a clicking noise of the tongue expressing disapproval.

indicators.note: the first half of the word is taken

parts.note: champignon is the French word for a mushroom

explanation.surface: A half serving of mushroom made into a puree.
explanation.definitionFit: Mush is any soft pulpy mass, and a puree is food pulped to that state.

clue.text: Copper probes where beer bottles are stored? Wrong

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so these letters go inside the phrase

parts.note: beer bottles are stored in a crate
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer investigates a beer store and gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman probing, but it is the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong is incorrect or not accurate.

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: the word for different sits outside the word say

parts.note: other means different

explanation.surface: A prophet, for example, looks very different on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is taken as written and put inside OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer foretells the future, which is what a prophet does.

indicators.note: bending back means the letters are read in reverse
the phrase steel bars is shortened at both ends, leaving letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A skilled worker bends cut-down steel bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' leaves ELBA within steel bars, and 'bending' turns it back; the blog calls bending an unusual reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able is skilled or competent at something, much like an expert.
